### Welcome

This is our Geocomputation lab on Employer-Household Dynamics. This is an R analysis [inspired by this post](https://walker-data.com/posts/lodes-2020/)

### Libraries

```{r}
library(lehdr)
library(tigris)
library(mapgl)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(mapview)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```

### Data

Our data is from the [Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LEHD)](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/) study from the US Census Bureau. When interacting with data like these, we should always think: "is there an r package that can make interacting with this data easier?". And the answer is yes!

The [lehdr package](https://jamgreen.github.io/lehdr/index.html) allows users to interface with the [Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LEHD)](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/) Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) dataset, returned as tidy data frames

```{r}
hi_od <- grab_lodes(
  state      = "hi",
  year       = 2022,
  lodes_type = "od",
  job_type   = "JT00",
  segment    = "S000",
  state_part = "main",
  agg_geo    = "tract",
  geometry   = TRUE
) |>
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "w_geometry")
```

How did this `grab_lodes()` function work

```{r}
?grab_lodes
```

What do these column names mean?

Each row is one home-tract-to-work-tract pair. The numbers count **jobs** (in your call, `JT00` means all jobs), so a person with two jobs can appear twice.

| Column | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `year` | Data year (2022) |
| `state` | State abbreviation |
| `w_tract` | GEOID of the **work** tract |
| `h_tract` | GEOID of the **home** tract |
| `S000` | Total jobs in this home-to-work flow |
| `SA01` | Jobs held by workers aged 29 or younger |
| `SA02` | Workers aged 30–54 |
| `SA03` | Workers aged 55 or older |
| `SE01` | Jobs earning \$1,250/month or less |
| `SE02` | \$1,251–\$3,333/month |
| `SE03` | More than \$3,333/month |
| `SI01` | Goods-producing industries (agriculture, mining, construction, manufacturing) |
| `SI02` | Trade, transportation and utilities |
| `SI03` | All other services (government, health, education, hospitality, etc.) |
| `w_geometry` / `h_geometry` | Tract polygons for the work and home ends |

### Analysis

Define destination point

```{r}
dest_point <- st_sfc(st_point(c(-157.9225, 21.3187)), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(hi_od))

# One row per work tract, keeping only the ID and its polygon
w_tracts <- hi_od[!duplicated(hi_od$w_tract), "w_tract"]

dest_geoid <- w_tracts$w_tract[lengths(st_intersects(w_tracts, dest_point)) > 0]
dest_geoid
```

Filter flows and turn into long

```{r}
top_commutes <- hi_od |>
  filter(w_tract == dest_geoid, S000 >= 25, h_tract != w_tract)

to_lonlat <- function(g) {
  g |>
    st_transform(26904) |>        # UTM 4N for accurate interior points
    st_point_on_surface() |>
    st_transform(4326) |>
    st_coordinates()
}

h_xy <- to_lonlat(top_commutes$h_geometry)
w_xy <- to_lonlat(top_commutes$w_geometry)

top_commutes <- top_commutes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>           # drops w_geometry (the active column)
  select(-h_geometry) |>          # h_geometry is a second sfc column, drop it too
  mutate(h_lon = h_xy[, 1], h_lat = h_xy[, 2],
         w_lon = w_xy[, 1], w_lat = w_xy[, 2])
```

Build curved arcs

```{r}
make_arc <- function(x1, y1, x2, y2, n = 60, curve = 0.25) {
  mx <- (x1 + x2) / 2; my <- (y1 + y2) / 2
  cx <- mx - (y2 - y1) * curve               # control point offset
  cy <- my + (x2 - x1) * curve
  t  <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  st_linestring(cbind(
    (1 - t)^2 * x1 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cx + t^2 * x2,
    (1 - t)^2 * y1 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cy + t^2 * y2
  ))
}

flows_sf <- top_commutes |>
  mutate(
    geometry = pmap(list(h_lon, h_lat, w_lon, w_lat), make_arc),
    tooltip  = paste0(S000, " commuters<br>from tract ", h_tract)
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(crs = 4326)

origins_sf <- top_commutes |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("h_lon", "h_lat"), crs = 4326)

dest_sf <- top_commutes |>
  slice(1) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("w_lon", "w_lat"), crs = 4326)

```

Map

```{r}
max_jobs <- max(flows_sf$S000)

m <- maplibre(
  style   = carto_style("positron"),
  center  = c(-157.98, 21.42),
  zoom    = 9.6,
  pitch   = 50,
  bearing = -20
) |>
  add_line_layer(
    id         = "flows",
    source     = flows_sf,
    line_color = interpolate(
      column = "S000",
      values = c(25, max_jobs),
      stops  = c("#f06400", "#00c800")     # orange -> green, echoing the original
    ),
    line_width = interpolate(
      column = "S000",
      values = c(25, max_jobs),
      stops  = c(1, 8)
    ),
    line_opacity = 0.8,
    tooltip      = "tooltip",
    hover_options = list(line_color = "#ffff00")
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id           = "origins",
    source       = origins_sf,
    circle_color = "#f06400",
    circle_radius = 3,
    circle_opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id                  = "destination",
    source              = dest_sf,
    circle_color        = "#00c800",
    circle_radius       = 8,
    circle_stroke_color = "white",
    circle_stroke_width = 2
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Commuters to the airport / JBPHH tract",
    values = c("Fewer", "More"),
    colors = c("#f06400", "#00c800"),
    type   = "continuous"
  )

m
```

### Your Turn

Challenge 1: Recreate [this figure](https://github.com/jamgreen/lehdr/blob/master/vignettes/figures/fig1_balt_self_containment.png) for Hawaii

```{r}
od_md <- grab_lodes(
  state      = "hi",
  year       = 2022,
  lodes_type = "od",
  job_type   = "JT00",
  segment    = "S000",
  state_part = "main",
  agg_geo    = "tract"
)

commute_md <- compute_commute_stats(od_md, agg_geo = "tract")

commute_md |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(self_containment)) |>
  dplyr::select(tract, workers_in, workers_out, net_flow, self_containment) |>
  head(10)

```

```{r}
hi_tracts <- tracts(state="hi", year = 2022, cb = TRUE)

map_hi <- hi_tracts |> 
  left_join(commute_md, by = c("GEOID" = "tract"))

mapview(map_hi, zcol = "self_containment")
```

Challenge 2: Recreate t[his figure](https://github.com/jamgreen/lehdr/blob/master/vignettes/figures/fig2_md_job_change.png) for a state of your choosing

```{r}
wac_md_panel <- grab_lodes(
  state      = "id",
  year       = c(2015, 2020),
  lodes_type = "wac",
  job_type   = "JT00",
  segment    = "S000",
  agg_geo    = "county"
)

change_md <- compute_lodes_change(
  wac_md_panel,
  geo_col      = "w_county",
  base_year    = 2015,
  compare_year = 2020,
  variables    = c("C000", "CE01", "CE02", "CE03")
)

change_md |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(C000_change)) |>
  dplyr::select(w_county, C000_base, C000_compare, C000_change, C000_pct_change) |>
  head(10)
```

```{r}
id_county <- counties(state = "id", year = 2020, cb = TRUE)

map_id <- id_county |> 
  left_join(change_md, by = c("GEOID" = "w_county"))

mapview(map_id, zcol = "C000_pct_change")
```

```{r}
wac_md <- grab_lodes(
  state      = "hi",
  year       = 2020,
  lodes_type = "wac",
  job_type   = "JT00",
  segment    = "S000",
  agg_geo    = "tract"
)

earn_shares <- compute_earnings_share(wac_md, type = "wac", geo_col = "w_tract")

# Counties with the highest share of low-wage jobs
earn_shares %>%
  arrange(desc(share_low)) %>%
  select(w_tract, share_low, share_mid, share_high) %>%
  head(10)
```

```{r}
earn_long <- compute_earnings_share(
  wac_md,
  type    = "wac",
  geo_col = "w_tract",
  output  = "long"
)

head(earn_long)
```

```{r}
hi_tract20 <- tracts(state="hi", year = 2020, cb = TRUE)

map_hi_in <- hi_tract20 |> 
  left_join(earn_shares, by = c("GEOID" = "w_tract"))
```

```{r}
mapview(map_hi_in, zcol = "share_high")
```

```{r}
m <- mapview(map_hi_in, zcol = "share_high")
m@map |> leaflet::fitBounds(-157.557814, 21.805664, -158.395249, 21.133741)
```
